Dublin; translated by Yeats as "savage indignation" (poem 256).
 245: see Yeats's note on The Winding Stair and Other Poems, p. In Christian
legend, the Veronica is a handkerchief or veil which a woman gave Christ to
wipe his face as he was on the way to Calvary; when he returned it, it bore
the imprint of his face.
 245.1: "The Heavenly Circuit" is the title of one of the sections (II.2) of the
Enneads of the Neoplatonic philosopher Plotinus (205-6g/7o): God is placed
at the center of the universe, with all things circling around him. According
to legend, the hair of Berenice II (ca. 273-221 B.C.), offered for the safe
return of her husband Ptolemy III (ca. 284-221 B.c.), king of Egypt, became
a constellation, Coma Berenices.
 245.2: the "Tent-pole of Eden" may be what Yeats described in a note to poem
64 as "the pole of the heavens, the ancient Tree of Life in many countries."
